character: Tilpey Cross is a city of readers, minds and shops on a grid by the lake: its Pokemon keep the hour, mind doors, sort books, serve food and perform on the corner, and the rest stare, nap, dance and play chess. Psychic and city Pokemon; no farm animal and nothing from the marsh or the garden.

workers.interact: The Abra is asleep. It has been reading all the same: the page turns by itself.
The Natu has not looked away from the spire's lens since you arrived. The instrument beside it ticks.
The Minccino sweeps the square's paving with its tail. It goes back over a stone you stepped on.
The Porygon counts everyone who goes into the department store. It has counted you twice.
The Kadabra sharpens the stationer's pencils by looking at them. The shavings come off in perfect spirals.
The Medicham breaks one board for the dojo's beginners, slowly, so they can see how. Then it waits for them to try.
The Bronzong keeps the square's hours. Nobody wound it; nobody remembers it being wrong.
The Indeedee brings plates out from the market kitchen. It knows what you ordered before you do.
The Exeggcute tend the physic garden's beds, all six at once, in six slightly different directions.
The Mr. Mime on the corner is pressing its hands against a wall that is not there. You walk round it anyway.
The Beheeyem carries the reading stall's books back up from the lake a few at a time. Its fingers blink when it thinks about the one it is holding.
The Wobbuffet minds the department store's side door. It does not stop anyone going in. It sends back anyone who pushes.
The Magnemite is fixing the street lamp. It has fixed this lamp every evening for a month.

pets.why: the pattern-reader's Meowstic, ears folded: they stay folded until it needs to know what you are thinking
the pattern-reader's Solosis, floating at shoulder height wherever she stops
the market counter's Skitty, chasing the counter's own string
the counter clerk's Wynaut, which agrees with everything the clerk says
the stationer's Hatenna, who hides under the stall whenever a customer is cross
the market kitchen's Glameow, sitting where the scraps land and looking as if it does not care
the physic gardener's Ralts, which hides behind her when anyone it does not know comes near

placed.why: hanging from the porch beam where a wind chime would be; it rings when the door opens
on the library's step, still as a statue, facing the observatory; the readers walk round it
asleep in the window, a faint pink mist on the glass
staring out of the cartographer's window at nothing, without blinking
on the fisher cottage's step, dripping from the lake
on the porch chair, asleep, which nobody remarks on
on the masons' roof; the masons say it was there when they built it
in the Mart's window, tinkling every time a customer leaves

situations.title: The staring contest in the square
situations.story: A Xatu and a Girafarig have been staring at each other in the square since morning, and a small crowd has gathered. The money is on the Girafarig: it has two heads.
situations.why: Tilpey Cross's own: a city of minds settles things by looking, and a city draws a crowd for anything

situations.title: Asleep on the observatory steps
situations.story: A Musharna is asleep on the observatory steps in a haze of pink dream mist. The Hypno and the Rellor next to it were not tired when they sat down.
situations.why: the observatory's south face, between it and the Centre; a hypnotist asleep is the joke

situations.title: The tea service in the masons' garden
situations.story: In the masons' back garden three Bronzor sit on the table like a tea service. The masons eat standing up.
situations.why: a back garden taken over: the three of one species ARE the situation, on a table behind the house

situations.title: The Spoink that will not stop
situations.story: Since dawn a Spoink has been bouncing outside the cartographer's door. A Grumpig sits beside it with its head in its hands.
situations.why: a Spoink's heart stops if it stops bouncing; the one that has grown out of it is tired

situations.title: The chess game by the library
situations.story: A Meditite and an Inkay play chess on a barrel by the library's door. The Inkay plays upside down, and is winning.
situations.why: the library's east door; a reading town's pastime

situations.title: The dance in Observatory Street
situations.story: On clear nights two Clefairy and a Cleffa dance in the street in front of the observatory. The astronomers time their readings by them.
situations.why: the gym street's west end, under the observatory; the moon is what the observatory looks at

situations.title: The voice in the armourer's chimney
situations.story: The armourer's family hear crying in their chimney every evening and have stopped lighting the fire. It is a Misdreavus sitting in the pot, and it is not crying: it is laughing at them.
situations.why: something in a chimney, in the town that listens: gym6_house_07's chimney stack is the cobblestone wall at (6255, 3420) whose top, at 102, stands two to four above the roof blocks round it (the template as placed, building top 103 feet y). The highest chimney in Tilpey Cross, seen from the east road

situations.title: The memory stone with a face
situations.story: Seven memory stones stand along the rows, each a stone the Rift left and what the town remembers of it. The one near the end of the east row has grown a face. It is a Spiritomb, and the readers say it remembers things nobody wrote down.
situations.why: beside sabrina_memory_stone_5 at (6290, 3453), on the plan's y 96: a town that keeps memory stones gets the one Pokemon that is bound to a keystone. Someone has left it candles
